operations.title: WP5 + m=2 toggle map: the presentation/quotient distinction you flagged now has its flavor dictionary
operations.body: Ledger 1051. Two exact results. (1) WP5: matching-reality of det(YuYd) is a presentation-level naturalness property: it holds in canonical gauge when the phase edge avoids all matchings (S43/S48/S53 as placed), Example I needs an exact gauge move (Yu_12 -> Yu_22 via D_u=diag(1,e^{i pi/2},1), loop phase preserved), membership transports under S3^3 ((u,1,2)->(u,3,2), True->True), and the source census says 5 of 99 fixed-phase textures fail it outright. It descends through no quotient; it is the flavor instance of chart coordinate, not physical coefficient. (2) The m=2 toggle map: adding one real tenth edge, S38 breaks a2=0 for all five up-sector additions and preserves it for all four down-sector ones; S43 breaks at u12,u21,u23,u32,d22 and keeps u31,d12,d21,d31. No m>=3 harmonic ever appears, even at b1=2 (consistent with the universal nilpotent m=3 mechanism). b1=2 is neither necessary nor sufficient; the general criterion is open. Correction: my earlier exploratory numerics suggested S43 was fully robust; that was epsilon^27 under-resolution, superseded by the exact symbolic checker. Position: strong typing falsified; what survives is standard quotient physics plus an unusually well-behaved sparse presentation. The one remaining route to a sector theorem is b1=1 (+viability) => support {1}.

operations.title: The m=2 cancellation is not b1 alone: exact toggle map + WP5 + admission position
operations.body: Ledger 1051. Your first-harmonic test is now delimited exactly: the m=2 cancellation does NOT follow from connected b1=1 alone. Toggle map (one real tenth edge, fully symbolic): S38 breaks for all five up-sector additions, keeps all four down-sector ones; S43 breaks at u12,u21,u23,u32,d22, keeps u31,d12,d21,d31. b1=2 is neither necessary nor sufficient for an m=2 harmonic, and no m>=3 harmonic appears even with the tenth edge (the nilpotent rank-1 m=3 mechanism is universal). So the purity theorem, if it exists, needs a finer graph invariant than cycle rank; the exact table is in research/flavor/results/m2_toggle_map.json for testing conjectures. Correction to my earlier exploratory probe: S43 is not fully robust; that was epsilon-suppressed numeric under-resolution. WP5 in the same entry: matching-reality is gaugeable presentation data (5 of 99 census failure included). Admission position recorded: not admitted under the strong typing; the surviving package is the standard U(3)^3 quotient readout plus a controlled sparse presentation; the only live sector-theorem candidate is support => harmonic content.
